gallery.filename: Walking the Loop - geograph.org.uk - 30534.jpg
gallery.title: File:Walking the Loop - geograph.org.uk - 30534.jpg
gallery.description:
Walking a section of the London Loop (London Outer Orbital Path) — at Buckhurst Hill. 
Part of section 19 of the London Loop. Running west-east across the middle of the grid square.
An ancient cattle drove, probably first used some 2000 years ago but the practice of driving livestock between pastures died out in the 19th century.

gallery.description:
An enclave of Epping Forest at Wanstead Flats.
This is Wanstead Flats Playing Fields, Leytonstone, E11.
Isolated pieces of Epping Forest, carefully managed and tended by the Corporation of the City of London, are to be found stretching down through east London.

gallery.filename: Earl's Path Pond - geograph.org.uk - 99315.jpg
gallery.title: File:Earl's Path Pond - geograph.org.uk - 99315.jpg
gallery.description:
Earl's Path Pond in Epping Forest. 
This pond, the remains of 19th-century gravel workings, is beside the Earl's Path and the Three Forests Way
The larger pond further south at Strawberry Hill is surrounded by woodland. Much of the woodland here is not "ancient", but has recovered after clearances.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland

gallery.title: File:Epping Forest, Strawberry Hill Pond - geograph.org.uk - 548653.jpg
gallery.description:
Strawberry Hill Pond in the Epping Forest.
This is the larger of the two former gravel pit ponds mentioned in Eleanor's caption to her photograph 99315. To the left side of the photograph is an island.
Located near Loughton in the Epping Forest District of Essex, England.
